fields.narrative_intro: *A gleeful person and an apoplectic person discuss ClawDOS at an airport gate where the flight has been delayed 6 hours.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
GLEEFUL PERSON: "ClawDOS runs Claude's live API on a 1981 IBM PC XT 5160."
APOPLECTIC PERSON: "The 4.77 MHz one?"
fields.panel2:
[build]
GLEEFUL PERSON: "It has 640K RAM, a WiFi SD card, and two assemblers."
APOPLECTIC PERSON: "A luxury setup for a machine born in 1981."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
GLEEFUL PERSON: "Claude wrote its 176 KB DOS prison itself."
APOPLECTIC PERSON: "The 8088 needs a bridge machine just to handle TLS."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The gate display reads “DELAYED 6 HOURS.” The XT sits behind bars; a tiny bridge computer in a TLS SECURITY vest holds its visitor badge. Both people stare.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
APOPLECTIC PERSON: "ClawDOS compiles its first program in 64 seconds."
GLEEFUL PERSON: "Our airline has been compiling one departure for six hours."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The XT flashes “READY” after 64 seconds; the gate board still says “DELAYED 6 HOURS.” The TLS bridge computer is first in the boarding line.]

narrative_summary: At a six-hour-delayed gate, ClawDOS's 64-second compile time makes the airline look like the slower computer.
rationale: Candidate 3 best converts the 64-second compile into an earned, story-specific metaphor: the airline has been “compiling” one departure for six hours. It uses the ClawDOS facts thoroughly while keeping the six-panel escalation and final visual coherent.
story_title: ClawDOS – An AI coding agent for DOS
place: at an airport gate where the flight has been delayed 6 hours
